transcript:
HEADER:
Date: 2025-12-10
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Amir Hassan (Redwood SE); Michael Chen (Aureus IT Security), Sara Gomez (Aureus Platform Eng), Ravi Patel (Aureus Cloud), Leah Ortiz (Aureus Compliance)

SUMMARY:
Quick security and compliance review focused on SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, and RBAC/least-privilege model. Customer has Okta and Azure AD in different business units; primary ask is how Redwood supports SCIM attributes, group sync, custom role mapping, audit logs and KMS-encrypted data at rest. Discussed testing plan and pilot timeline.

TOPICS COVERED:
- SAML SSO flows, IdP metadata, ACS URLs
- SCIM provisioning attributes, group sync, deprovisioning behavior
- RBAC role model, least-privilege mappings, admin separation
- Audit logs, retention, and export paths to SIEM
- Data residency & KMS / envelope encryption basics for Private deployments
- Next steps and pilot coordination

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have around 45 minutes, this is Jordan from Redwood, with Priya and Amir who are our solutions folks. Michael, Sara, Ravi, Leah from Aureus, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Michael Chen: Yep thanks, we have a few separate groups, trying to lock down how SSO and provisioning will work before we start a pilot. Primary concerns are least privilege, deprovisioning, and audit trails.
[00:25] Priya Nair: Great, so we'll walk through our SAML and SCIM support, show how group-to-role mappings work, and then talk about audit logs and encryption. Quick note, apologies in advance for any auto-transcript weirdness, sometimes acronyms are munged.
[00:38] Sara Gomez: No worries, that's fine. We use Okta for most teams, but the trading floor uses Azure AD; we may need multi-IdP support or a single IdP in front.
[00:48] Amir Hassan: Redwood supports multiple IdPs per account, and you can configure routes per org or per route, so you could have Azure AD mapped to specific teams. On SCIM we support group sync and full user provisioning/deprovisioning, SCIM v2.
[00:59] Ravi Patel: How does deprovisioning behave? If a user is removed from Okta group, are tokens revoked immediately?
[01:07] Priya Nair: Good question. By default we mark the user as disabled on sync, and we can optionally revoke active sessions and API keys via the provisioning hook. There is a setting in the Admin Console to enable immediate session termination. It's eventual consistent within a few seconds to a minute depending on load.
[01:25] Leah Ortiz: For compliance we need a tamper-evident audit trail. What fields are in the audit log and how long can we retain them?
[01:34] Jordan Lee: Our audit logs include user, actor, action, resource, timestamp, and HTTP metadata. Retention by default is 90 days, but for Enterprise/Private we support extended retention and can stream logs to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) via secure forwarding.
[01:50] Michael Chen: Is streaming push-only or can we pull logs via API?
[01:55] Amir Hassan: You can pull via API or configure log forwarding. For Private deployments customers often push logs to a collector in their VPC.
[02:04] Sara Gomez: About RBAC we need a least-privilege model so that devs cannot change billing or rotate keys, we also need a separate admin for audit and compliance.
[02:13] Priya Nair: Our Roles model supports built-in roles and custom roles. Built-ins include Admin, Developer, ReadOnly, BillingAdmin. You can create a custom role scoped to actions like model-deploy, key-rotate, view-logs. We'll share a recommended mapping.
[02:27] Michael Chen: Can we scope roles to projects or routes? We want devs to only access specific routes and models.
[02:33] Priya Nair: Yes roles can be scoped to projects and per-route permissions. We also support resource-level tagging which lets you apply policies by tag.
[02:41] Ravi Patel: For SSO, what metadata do you need? SAML assertion attributes? Audience, NameID?
[02:48] Amir Hassan: Minimal: IdP metadata XML or SAML metadata URL, ACS URL (we'll provide), Entity ID, and usually an attribute for email or username. For SCIM we recommend synchronizing group membership and include attributes: userName, id, displayName, emails, and optional custom attributes for department/team. We'll attach our SCIM attribute mapping doc.
[03:06] Sara Gomez: How about SCIM group-to-role mapping? We have AD groups representing teams, we want group membership to map to roles in Redwood automatically.
[03:15] Priya Nair: You can map groups to roles for example, AD group "aureus-devs" => Redwood role Developer scoped to project X. We also support precedence rules and a default role for provisioned users.
[03:26] Michael Chen: If someone leaves the bank and their Okta account is deactivated, we want immediate deprovisioning and API key invalidation is that supported in the hosted offering or only Private?
[03:37] Jordan Lee: Hosted supports immediate deprovisioning and session termination via SCIM hooks too; however, some enterprises prefer Private because they want the control of KMS and stricter network egress policies. For token revocation we do support revoking active API keys on user disable event in both Hosted and Dedicated.
[03:56] Leah Ortiz: Encryption at rest do you support customer-managed keys?
[04:00] Amir Hassan: Yes. For Private deployments we integrate with BYOK via customer KMS/HSM (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP CMEK). For Hosted we use Redwood-managed keys by default but offer CMKs for enterprise plans in Dedicated/Private.
[04:15] Ravi Patel: Can you provide key rotation logs and attestations? Compliance will require rotation history.
[04:20] Priya Nair: We maintain key rotation events in audit logs and can provide rotation metadata. For Private we can expose KMS CloudTrail events in your account.
[04:30] Michael Chen: Data residency, can we ensure data for EU customers stays in EU regions?
[04:35] Jordan Lee: Yes, we support region pinning for data residency; with Private you can ensure all compute and storage remain in customer region. Hosted API can be pinned to region endpoints too.
[04:45] Sara Gomez: A question about SCIM attributes do you support custom attributes and how are they mapped to roles?
[04:51] Amir Hassan: We support custom attributes. The SCIM mapping UI lets you map custom attributes to user metadata fields and then use those fields in mapping rules for roles. The mapping engine supports simple expressions and group membership checks.
[05:03] Michael Chen: What about provisioning errors? How will we see failures if the SCIM sync can't create users due to schema mismatch?
[05:10] Priya Nair: Sync errors are surfaced in the Admin Console with error codes and the raw SCIM response. We also send webhook notifications to a configured ops channel and write entries to the audit log.
[05:20] Ravi Patel: Are service accounts and machine users supported? We sometimes need machine users for CI jobs but we don't want them to have broad privileges.
[05:28] Amir Hassan: Yes, we support machine users with scoped API keys and policies. Machine users can be created via API or via provisioning and you can scope keys to specific routes, model sets, or rate limits.
[05:40] Jordan Lee: Quick interjection on least-privilege mapping we typically recommend starting with three roles: ReadOnly, Developer (no billing or key rotation), and Admin. Create a BillingAdmin if finance needs access. We'll share a template.
[05:52] Leah Ortiz: Does Redwood support SCIM incremental syncs or only full push?
[05:57] Priya Nair: SCIM is incremental we support delta syncs and list-based queries as per SCIM v2. Deprovision events are delivered as provisioning deletes or by changing group membership.
[06:08] Michael Chen: For SAML assertions, do you require encrypted assertions or is signing sufficient?
[06:13] Amir Hassan: Signing is required; encrypted assertions are optional but supported if your IdP requires it. We can handle either, but signing only is the common path.
[06:22] Sara Gomez: On audit logs, can we search by user and export as CSV for audits?
[06:28] Jordan Lee: Yes, Admin Console supports search and export. For large volumes we recommend log forwarding to your SIEM and using the SIEM for queries and retention.
[06:36] Ravi Patel: We need an approval workflow for new role grants do you have an RBAC change approval process?
[06:43] Priya Nair: We don't have a built-in approver workflow today, but our audit logs capture the grant event and you can integrate with your internal ticketing or use a webhook to require an external approval step. This is a common ask, we can discuss roadmap.
[06:57] Michael Chen: Can we set session TTLs and enforce MFA from IdP?
[07:03] Amir Hassan: Session TTLs are configurable, and MFA should be enforced by your IdP during SAML auth; Redwood respects the authentication during the SAML assertion.
[07:12] Leah Ortiz: Regarding segregation of duties, can we create scoped admin roles per environment (prod vs staging)?
[07:18] Priya Nair: Yes, you can scope roles to environments and projects, which helps with separation of duties.
[07:25] Sara Gomez: A practical thing how long would it take to get a pilot running with Okta integration and 20 pilot users?
[07:30] Jordan Lee: Typically 1-2 weeks from kick-off: configure SAML, set up SCIM, run a sync, and validate role mappings. If you need Private deployment or custom KMS, add provisioning time.
[07:41] Michael Chen: Are there any limitations on SCIM groups size or number of users?
[07:45] Amir Hassan: No hard limit for enterprise customers; large directories may require pagination handling which we support. We'll provide guidance for large-scale syncs.
[07:55] Ravi Patel: For the pilot we need a list of required SAML attributes and our Okta admin will need ACS/Entity. Please send the metadata.
[08:02] Priya Nair: We'll send the ACS URL and the metadata XML and a checklist.
[08:07] Jordan Lee: We'll also attach our RBAC template and example group mappings to get you started.
[08:12] Sara Gomez: Can you confirm the API key rotation policy and if you can prevent admins from creating long-lived keys?
[08:18] Amir Hassan: You can set max TTLs and require rotation frequency. We also support policy-driven key lifetimes for machine users. Admins with proper permission can create keys but you can limit that capability to BillingAdmin or SecurityAdmin roles.
[08:30] Michael Chen: Anything on compliance certifications SOC 2?
[08:34] Jordan Lee: We are SOC 2 compliant; we can share our SOC 2 Type II report under NDA, and we have ISO plans in the roadmap if you need that detail.
[08:44] Leah Ortiz: We'll need the SOC 2 report and a data flow diagram for our security review.
[08:49] Jordan Lee: Noted, we'll share the SOC 2 docs and a standard data flow diagram.
[08:55] Michael Chen: One edge-case: some contractors don't have corporate emails can we provision accounts with non-corporate emails and then map them to AD groups?
[09:03] Priya Nair: You can provision external emails, but for SCIM-based syncs we recommend using corporate identities for lifecycle automation. You can create manual accounts for contractors if needed.
[09:12] Ravi Patel: If we want to test Private deployment later, what are network connectivity expectations?
[09:16] Amir Hassan: For Private we support two models: customer-hosted control plane or a dedicated VPC peering arrangement. We'll share a network checklist with required egress endpoints and port lists.
[09:28] Jordan Lee: Okay, we're about 35 minutes in; quick recap of next steps and owners. Priya will send SCIM guide and sample manifest; Jordan will send RBAC mapping template and SOC 2 artifact request; Michael/Ravi will provide pilot users and IdP metadata.
[09:43] Michael Chen: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:46] Sara Gomez: Thanks, appreciate it.
[09:48] Amir Hassan: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email and link the docs.
[09:51] Jordan Lee: End call.
